messages:
Incident Bot: Pager: HIGH — multiple GPU nodes reporting container crashes on runtime v2.4. Error: 'CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered'. Paging @Sam (oncall).

PagerDuty Bot: Pager triggered for service: redwood-runtime-gpu. Incident created: INC-20260315-4783.

Sam (oncall): oncall here, seeing spikes in pod restarts. attaching recent kube events + error lines. will start triage.

Sam (oncall): logs: ```
E CudaRuntime: call=cudaMemcpy H2D failed: an illegal memory access was encountered (77)
stack: runtime_kernel.cu:142:
  fused_attention_kernel+0x1f3
  launch_kernel+0x8b
  dispatch_kernel+0x45
```

Maria (eng-sre): can you paste node kernel/driver versions? any recent node upgrades?

Sam (oncall): nodes: gpu-1: kernel 6.1.41, nvidia-driver 525.78.01; gpu-2: kernel 6.1.41, nvidia-driver 525.78.01; started ~25m ago after an ASG rolling update.

Jae (infra): we rolled a node-image update 27m ago that updated the kernel/driver ABI. I'm seeing sporadic node flaps in the autoscale group: `InstanceTerminating` -> quick rejoin -> pod eviction loop.

Alex (eng-runtime): Noted. We shipped a fused-kernel optimization in runtime v2.4 yesterday that changes memory alignment for KV cache buffers. Hypothesis: new kernel/driver + fused kernel code -> misaligned access occasionally.

Maria (eng-sre): that matches: illegal memory access often due to out-of-bounds or misaligned pointers in custom kernels. Two mitigation paths: (A) roll back node image to previous driver, (B) disable fused-kernel path in runtime to force fallback to safe kernels. Both have tradeoffs.

Sam (oncall): immediate mitigation: cordon new nodes and migrate traffic to stable pool. executing now.

Sam (oncall): cmds: ```
kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu-rolling -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

Jae (infra): cordoned 3 nodes (gpu-rolling-1..3). triggering scale up of stable-gpu pool by +4 instances to absorb evicted pods.

Customer Success (Lina): CS: immediate customer impact summary: ~12% of hosted requests failing with 500 across 03:10-03:40 UTC. Customers with dedicated pools unaffected. Preparing outbound to top 3 accounts.

Alex (eng-runtime): I can patch a runtime flag to disable fused kernels per-deployment without full rollback. Patch: `RUNTIME_ENABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=false`. Pushing a canary change to 10% traffic to confirm.

Sam (oncall): apply env patch to runtime deployment for canary: ```kubectl set env deployment/runtime -n prod RUNTIME_ENABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=false --record```

Maria (eng-sre): monitor: error-rate on canary pods dropped to baseline in ~45s. Good sign. but still seeing restarts on older pods that landed on updated nodes.

Jae (infra): starting rolling rollback of node image for nodepool gpu-rolling -> previous AMI (ami-20250202). will drain and replace instances gradually. ETA ~25m.

PagerDuty Bot: Acknowledged by Sam (oncall). Priority set to P1 until either (1) node image rollback completes and error rate stabilizes, or (2) we fully disable fused-kernel across prod.

Sam (oncall): doing handoff to Maria for the next 90m window. Maria, you own the incident from here. Key context: cordoned new nodes, canary with fused-kernel disabled shows improvement, rollback in progress.

Maria (eng-sre): taking over — thanks Sam. checklist: (1) finish node rollback, (2) disable fused kernel cluster-wide if rollback stalls, (3) monitor model latency/cost. Posting runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-kernel-fault

Alex (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a follow-up runtime patch to add a safe-alignment assert and fallback path. Also starting a debug build to reproduce locally with the updated driver stack.

Jae (infra): node rollback completed for 6/7 nodes; one remaining due to a stuck termination (AWS side). Kube events show pods rescheduling to stable nodes, restart rate down from 18% -> 0.8%.

Customer Success (Lina): CS: initial notices sent to top 3 impacted accounts, showing mitigation steps. Will hold broader comms until we confirm return to baseline.

Maria (eng-sre): verified metrics: 5xx rate back to 0.5% (normal ~0.2%). Latency unchanged. I'll keep this open for 1hr for regression monitoring. Creating incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-20260315-4783/postmortem

Sam (oncall): thanks team. handing off final watch to Alex for runtime follow-up. I remain reachable for evictions.

Alex (eng-runtime): follow-up items added to runtime backlog: (a) add defensive alignment checks, (b) extend CI to test kernels against driver matrix, (c) consider turning fused-kernel flag OFF by default until driver matrix validated.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-20260315-4783 status -> mitigated. Root-cause candidate: misaligned memory access in fused attention CUDA kernel under specific kernel/driver combination introduced by node-image update. Postmortem assigned to Maria + Alex.
